statement: On a number line, 20 is exactly halfway between 26 and another number. What is the other number?

choices.misconception: I gave the gap from 20 to 26 instead of a number on the line.
I counted back 6 numbers from 20 but said 20 as the first one.
I found the number halfway between 20 and 26 instead.
I added 20 and 26 together instead of using the gap.

hints: Halfway means the same distance on both sides. Find how far 26 is from 20, then go the same distance from 20 the other way.
26 is 6 more than 20, so the other number is 6 less than 20.

solutions.reliable: 26 is 6 steps above 20. The middle number must be the same distance from both ends, so the other number is 6 steps below 20: 20 - 6 = 14. Check: halfway between 14 and 26 is 20. The idea to keep: the middle of two numbers is equally far from each, so a known end and the middle tell you the other end.
solutions.elegant: Draw 20 in the middle with a jump of 6 to the right to reach 26. Copy the same jump to the left and you land on 14.

whyOnTest: Working from the middle out to an end checks that you understand halfway as equal distances, not as a sum to halve.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
